themes: T1 Spells do not meet the world: talent shots skip the end of their step and pass through walls at 37 fps or more (hell_talents.gd:459, checked: range(1, steps) never tests the end point). Talent explosions ignore props and breakables, impacts land at a guessed point, and talent hits get no hit reaction (F23, F47, F49, F34, F25).

T2 Two matter worlds plus painted copies: the hero kit and attacks run their own Particles instance. hell_game.embers, StoryHero._bits, RigFx, gold coins and wreck shards each have their own, simpler physics. Ultimates and talent pixels paint drops, shards and embers next to their particle versions (F0/F32, F11, F51, F52, F54, F29, F30, F31).

T3 Drawing code changes gameplay, which breaks the deterministic-footprint rule: residue pools placed by talent_fx with a random length hurt and trip the caster, and particles.freeze_liquids turns gameplay poison and blood into Glatteis (F24, F17; F15 and F28 caution).

T4 The picture contradicts the rules: pool reactions are drawn against ElementRules.top (hidden fire still burns, a 'safe' crust still burns, poison hisses instead of exploding). Overlapping pools are drawn by spawn order. Reactions throw the wrong matter, poison gas burns from its centroid and comes back whole, and the Krypta's Moder runs the lava code (F12, F21, F13, F14, F26, F48).

T5 Contact physics between materials is missing: gas over lava or fire, poison on lava and residue never react. Ice never thaws on its own, every gas moves the same way, and the necromancer's poison is a painted circle (F15, F18, F16, F28, F19).

T6 One rule for all particle physics: every material bounces like rubber. There is no air drag or buoyancy, comet arcs are integrated with Euler, the wells miss their core, walls, gates and props are not solid to matter, blasts and wells act through walls, hitting the cap pops or teleports matter, and particles ignore the depth order (F1, F2, F9, F4, F8, F50, F5, F6, F7, F3).

T7 Frame-rate dependence: knockback decays per frame, gas parting is applied per call, trails emit per draw, ambient embers and vents spawn per frame, and wall gaps and core misses grow with v·dt (F35, F22, F10, F51, F53, F8, F9, F4, F57).

T8 Bodies: pushes are assigned instead of added and point away from the hero instead of the blast. They ignore mass, keep velocity into walls and stop dead on ice the same as on stone. Corpses freeze and vanish, and flights stop dead and snap upright (F37, F44, F46, F40, F36, F41, F45).

T9 The Frostgruft lags behind Krypta and Hölle because it has no monster runtime: no pool reactions, ragdolls fly in random directions through walls, contact does not knock the hero, boss pushes teleport him, there is no wading, and freezing only happens in the other worlds (F20, F38, F39, F43, F55, F17).

T10 Static world objects: traps and gates switch by swapping sprites, torches are sealed animation loops, and settled debris never moves again. On hero death everything freezes except the particles (F53, F56, F54, F42).

T11 Owned by the brother (saidPC), needs his OK: snow does not melt from fire or blasts, the wind exists only in the screen overlay, there is no skid entry point for monsters, and the flame tip is not exposed (F57, F58, plus the brother's parts of F16, F55 and F56).

Phase 1 picture: Hölle. A Feuerball talent hits a wall beside lava, with a barrel and an imp in reach. The burst sits on the wall face, chips fly off the wall normal, the hero's embers hiss out in the lava instead of lying on it, the barrel shatters along the blast, the imp bleeds from the talent hit, and no fire puddle is left under the mage.

Phase 2 picture: Krypta room with Moder. A fire talent ignites a Giftwolke. A flame front runs through it puff by puff and leaves a fireball, embers, a scorch star and rising smoke, with no green veil. The Moder bubbles olive with miasma. A water puddle over burning ground still shows the fire.

Phase 3 picture: Hölle. A blast next to a closed portcullis and a pillar. Drops splat with crowns and stick to the gate bars, smoke rises and widens, debris strikes the wall face, matter behind the pillar is hidden by it, gold bounces off the wall, a shard sinks into the lava with a plop, and the talent's matter is particles only.

Phase 4 picture: Frostgruft. A Rage or Urknall throw across Glatteis. Bodies glide, then roll back upright. Ragdoll parts fly away from the blow and bounce off walls. Fire melts a snowman's frost pool rim first, with steam, into water that monsters slide and wade through.

backlog.title: Talent shots stop at the first wall and burst at the contact point
backlog.what_player_sees_now: At 60 fps a talent shot never meets a wall: talent_blocked tests only interior samples, and none when the step is under 12 px. The shot turns invisible inside the wall, comes out in the next room and hits monsters behind the wall. talent_fx guesses the impact from the shot vanishing (talent_fx.gd:777), so the boom, shatter and residue appear where its 1.6 s life ends, often in mid-air about 700 px away. At low fps the shot just vanishes at the stone with no chips. MageBolt bursts inside the wall cell (mage_bolt.gd:146).
backlog.after: _step_bullets gets its own sweep: samples every 6 px or less including the end point, then a bisection to the contact point and a normal from story_feel's side probes. The shot ends there. A shot_ends {at, normal, talent, style} list in the snapshot replaces talent_fx's guess, so the burst, sparks and shards fly off the wall normal from the wall face. The wall is worn through wreck.hit_line, which also breaks a smashable prop in the way; an unbroken breakable calls _hit_breakable. There is no extra feel.wall_hit (it would double the matter). In hell_game the MageBolt position is set to the contact before burst(). talent_blocked stays unchanged for the melee line-of-sight check.

backlog.title: One particle world for hero attacks, the kit and talents
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Hero fireballs, fist bursts and shot impacts use a second Particles instance (story_skill_fx.gd:46, story_hero.gd:156). It has no sink, no liquids and no sound. Embers, soot and frost lie on top of Hölle lava, and the hero's floor marks are drawn over lava pools, gas, the ice slab and his own shadow. Blasts and the Singularität move the world's debris but not the hero's debris next to it. Hero matter makes no landing sound. Trails spawn once per draw call, so a 144 Hz screen shows 2.4× the trail of a 60 Hz one (skill_fx.gd:220, attack_fx.gd:366).
backlog.after: skill_fx.particles, skill_fx.skill.particles and attack.particles point to g.feel.feedback.particles. A `shared` flag skips the second update, draw and clear calls. embers(), frost(), stain() and scatter() check sinks(), so the hero's embers hiss out in lava and his marks lie under the liquid surfaces. Every blast and well moves all matter, landings make sounds, and there is one budget (max_particles raised to about 900). Trails are emitted from update time per distance flown, so they look the same at any refresh rate.

backlog.title: Talent hits throw the target's own matter; talent swings clang on walls
backlog.what_player_sees_now: _damage_enemy never calls g.feel.on_hit (hell_talents.gd:475). Wutschlag, Schildstoß, Schnittwunde, Fächerschnitt, Erdspalter, the dashes, every nova and Durchschuss show only the slash sheet and a white flash: no blood, bone chips, slime or spark from the target. Dash matter appears at the dash start in the class colour. Talent swings into walls are silent.
backlog.after: Each talent hit runs story_feel.on_hit with the material's sound only once (the feedback path plays it). Blood drops splat, bone chips settle, slime splashes and the target squashes. A talent_swing_wall hook in talent_combat's melee branch and channel swing (:692) clangs on walls and props. Dashes raise dust along their path, and shot hits throw less matter.

backlog.title: Drawing code stops changing gameplay: residue pools and rime freeze become looks only
backlog.what_player_sees_now: A Feuerball into a nearby wall leaves fire that burns the Feuermagier himself ('im Feuer verbrannt'). Every Wirbelsturm or Blutiger Schrei leaves a blood slick under the berserker, even with no hit. A Frostlanze on a wall leaves Glatteis, and a fizzled void shot leaves a pool that hurts and silences. These pools come from draw passes with a random length (talent_fx.gd:342/959). The Blizzard's rime (particles.freeze_liquids → pool_field.freeze_near) silently turns a monster's poison puddle into slippery ice that no longer poisons, but only in Krypta and Hölle.
backlog.after: Talent residue lives in its own visual-only PoolPaint: it shows, rings and wets soles, but never hurts or trips anyone. particles.freeze_liquids calls a new pool_paint.freeze_look that adds drawing-only ice and never writes pool_field. Gameplay ice comes only from story_elements.frost_at. Residue that should act in gameplay is decided under D1 and laid later from talent_combat events, sparing the caster.
backlog.effort: S for visual-only; M if residue becomes gameplay (D1)
backlog.risk: medium (removes damage and slips that players currently get)

backlog.title: Talent blasts bite walls and break props, crates and urns
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Meteor, Nova and talent explosions call only _element and never wreck.blast (talent_combat.gd:2499), so candles, bones and urns beside a Meteor stay whole. Crates, urns and barrels break only from the hero's swing and shots. A fireball or boss slam blows the candle beside a barrel to shards while the barrel does not even shake (story_wreck.gd:226).
backlog.after: hell_talents walks the snapshot events once per id. Explosion, nova and impact events with r >= blast.min_radius call wreck.blast and the breakables hook. Pyro-shot events that _explode already blasted are tagged and skipped. Breakables in reach shake and chip, and those in the core shatter along hit_dir. Enemy blasts and owner-0 poison explosions only shake and chip them (D6).
backlog.risk: medium (seals and skull heaps take blast hits)

backlog.title: Knockback distance and the Rage slam window no longer depend on the frame rate
backlog.what_player_sees_now: The push decays by 0.86 per frame (motion_kit.gd:163). A Rage throw flies about 111 px at 60 Hz, 46 px at 144 Hz and 223 px at 30 Hz. The slam only counts within about 72 px of a wall at 60 Hz, but 30 px at 144 Hz. A sword knock moves an enemy 18 px at 60 Hz and 7 px at 144 Hz.
backlog.after: step_body uses push*pow(decay, dt*60), which keeps today's 60 Hz tuning exactly. It returns push_in and hit, so check_slam (story_hero.gd:222) stops hardcoding /0.86. Throws and slam windows are the same on every machine. R23 and R27 build on this.

backlog.title: Reactions throw their own matter: explosion, boiling, rain and thaw
backlog.what_player_sees_now: A poison explosion is 22 green sparks bouncing on the floor plus a flash disc (story_elements.gd:411). In the Frostgruft it is only a shake and a flash. Boiling throws 5 frost-blue sparks. Condensing steam throws frost sparks upward before a puddle spreads from its middle. A thaw is 4 frost sparks.
backlog.after: One helper that needs only _particles()/_pscale(), so it works in all three worlds. An explosion is fire_burst, tumbling embers, a scorch_star and a smoke cloud left behind (the old crypt pattern). Boiling is dense steam puffs rising for about 1 s. Rain is drops falling from the cloud's height over its area, building the puddle as they land through drop_landed. A thaw hisses and drips. The four frost _burst_in calls go away.

backlog.title: Ignited poison gas burns as a front, and burnt gas stays gone
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Fire tests a cloud by its spawn centroid and radius (gas_field.gd:395-407). A cloud spread down a corridor goes off in its middle, and fire at its visible tail can miss. The green veil fades for 1.4 s and is blown outward by its own blast. A burnt or swallowed Giftwolke comes back whole on the next frame through GasField.sync (gas_field.gd:107), can explode again and keeps poisoning.
backlog.after: GasField.ignite gives each puff burn_at = now + distance/speed on the host clock. Each puff flashes to flame (fire_burst) and becomes dark smoke, and damage applies once per cloud. Ignition tests real thickness (gas.thickness >= dense_from). end_cloud records the key as spent so sync never re-adds it, and the talent zone ends with the gas (tc end_zone).
backlog.risk: medium (the explosion moves to where the gas really is)

backlog.title: The pool picture shows what the rules do
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Blood or water over burning ground hides the fire while the hero keeps burning, and the fire stays invisible after the blood dries. Poison touching fire hisses like steam. Blood, poison or water on lava paints a dark crust that reads as safe but still burns (pool_paint.gd:1605-1661). Overlapping pools are drawn in spawn order (pool_paint.gd:446): clean water is drawn over the poison that is poisoning you, and blood in water is a hard red sheet.
backlog.after: The draw loop and liquid_at are sorted by ElementRules priority, so the material that acts is drawn on top. A liquid over fire is hidden and hisses at the rim instead of hiding the fire. Liquids on lava hiss away without crust, and crust is drawn only where story_elements.crusted() is true. Poison meeting fire or lava flares as flame. Drawing-only mixes (bloodwater, toxicwater) in vfx_pools.json tint water.

backlog.title: The Krypta's Moder is cold sludge, not lava
backlog.what_player_sees_now: The green Moder bubbles orange-white lava domes at 9/s (hell_game.gd:3352-3385). They burst into orange glut drops that lie as embers and cool to soot. Liquids on it hiss and crust (story_feel.gd:786). Shockwaves throw orange lava tongues (hell_monsters.gd:3150). A poison puddle on Moder explodes and water boils (story_elements.gd:351). Krypta and Frostgruft debris sinks into tiles 2/3 with a heat glow, so even glaze ice swallows debris (story_wreck.gd:918).
backlog.after: theme.liquid.material plus a hell_game._floor_mat() helper. Moder shows slow olive bubbles that pop into miasma wisps, green drops that lie as wet poison pixels, ripples and a sluggish slosh, with no embers, soot, steam or crust. Debris sinks into Moder without glow, and glaze ice never swallows debris. Puddle gameplay on Moder follows D3.

backlog.title: Each gas moves like its material, parting is per second, and shots cut lanes
backlog.what_player_sees_now: All five gases share one set of constants (gas_field.gd:264). Boiling steam lies on the floor for about 6 s like poison, frost mist does not sink, and smoke behaves like poison. part() runs once per frame with no dt (gas_field.gd:227), so the hero parts gas 2.4× harder at 144 fps, and his poison dose and view range depend on the fps. cut() is only used by the old dungeon, so arrows, fireballs and monster shots fly through clouds without leaving a lane.
backlog.after: vfx_gas.json gets per-material physics (swell, thin, spread, drift, hold). Steam swells and is gone in about 1.5 s with a drawn rise, smoke swells and lingers, poison creeps low into corners, and frost mist spreads wide and flat. part() and cut() take dt. Every eshot and talent bullet inside a cloud cuts a lane that closes behind it, and the monsters' part radius scales with m.r.
backlog.risk: medium (poison dose at high fps changes)

backlog.title: Pools land at impact and shrink while they drain
backlog.what_player_sees_now: A thrown poison potion shatters, nothing lies there for about 0.33 s, then the full 5000-cell pool appears in one frame together with its splash (pool_field.gd:181, timings from the zone start). A pool drained by a void mouth stays full while its motes stream away, then vanishes rim first in 0.35 s.
backlog.after: Threaded pools count their cell births from max(start, commit). That is still deterministic, so the pool spreads after it shows, and the crown and drops play at impact. PoolField.retime(key, now, new_end, toward) shrinks a drained pool toward the mouth, far rim first.

backlog.title: Contact reactions for any matter, whatever made it (after D2)
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Between attacks only two checks run: water against lava circles, and puddle centres on a tile-2 floor (story_elements.gd:178/349/441). Poison gas drifting over Hölle lava or a fire puddle never ignites. A poison puddle on lava does nothing. Steam over Frostgruft ice never condenses, and frost mist over water never freezes.
backlog.after: A 0.2 s contact pass checks a few gas puffs per cloud against materials_at and the hot floor, and calls fire_at, frost_at or condense. PoolField.pools_near returns both zones and field pools, so the same meeting always reacts the same way. Residue stays out per D1. Depends on R4 and R8.
backlog.risk: medium (gameplay change, reverses the 2026-10-30 'visible only' decision)

backlog.title: Seuchenfeld becomes real poison gas over a pool, Seelensturm a soul well
backlog.what_player_sees_now: The necromancer's plague is a see-through circle (alpha 0.16) with a looping poison sheet (talent_fx.gd:1741). It never spreads, is never blown away, never explodes and lays no pool, yet it poisons everything in r every second. Seelensturm is a sprite loop.
backlog.after: Plague is spreading poison gas over a poison pool of about 0.8 r. It parts around bodies, is blown by blasts and burns as a front (R8). It spares its owner through an owner field in the cloud and pool records that StoryExposureHost filters on. Seelensturm swirls soul motes on a particles.well with suck=false. The sprite stays only when gas is null. Depends on R4 and R8.

backlog.title: Each material lands its own way; buoyancy and air drag
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Every particle mode shares one contact rule (particles.gd:1872). Drops hop and roll 5-10 px like beads. Flames and smoke bounce off walls. Ice shards, rubble and skulls skate across lava and only vanish where they come to rest. Water drops vanish in lava silently, kicked wet pixels just disappear, and pool pixels fly off as hard chips. There is no drag on vz (particles.gd:1905): flakes speed up while falling, smoke, steam and embers accelerate upward forever as rigid columns, and motes 'rise' by sliding north into walls (particles.gd:1394/1497). A flame's glow stays white-yellow at full strength, then pops off (particles.gd:2214).
backlog.after: Per-mode contact data in vfx_particles.json (wall: bounce, slide or stick; floor: bounce or splat) with a separate `stuck` flag, not `landed`. Drops splat on first contact with a short streak and a 1-2 px crown, ring into pools and paint wall faces. Flames and smoke creep along walls. Matter that touches lava at z<=0 sinks at once with a hiss or a plop (the skull branch too). vz gets air drag with a terminal speed: flakes drift down, smoke widens, embers rise then fall as they cool, and motes rise in height. Flame glow cools along the ramp. Comet modes keep air 0.

backlog.title: Walls, gates and props stop matter; blasts and wells cannot act through walls
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Blood drops, chips, shards and rubble sail through closed portcullises, pillars, braziers, chests and crates and settle under or behind them (particles.gd:177, story_feel.gd:791). Gas does stop there. Debris turns away before the wall: 4 crypt px short at 60 fps, up to 13 at the dt clamp. It slips through corners, and matter born inside a wall passes through it. A blast or the Singularität makes debris in the next room jump, or drags pixels from behind a wall (particles.gd:1609-1727, 930-950, 1272-1292).
backlog.after: Closed doors, solid prop footprints and unbroken breakables are erased from the particles' walkable cells and restored when a door opens or a crate breaks. Drops splat on the gate bars and debris bounces off pillars. Wall hits clamp to the crossed cell face at any fps, corners reflect on the smaller penetration, and matter born in a wall leaves on the open side. kick, blow, _suck and the wells use a cached DDA _sees(), so matter behind a wall stays put.

backlog.title: Talent looks become particles: only shapes stay painted
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Erdspalter's slam plays the old Blutrausch blood fountain (talent_ults.gd:78/529). Eissturz, Blutwelle, Feuersturm, the Meteor call, the flask and the Klingensturm finale paint drops, shards and embers on top of their particles or instead of them. A talent shot's embers travel with the ball and never fall behind (talent_pixels.gd:915). Impact drops and motes are painted next to their particle versions, and the Glutkette's flames hang where the target was. Schildwall and Seelenschild shatter into ice, and stone domes chip ice (talent_fx.gd:1262/2368). Pfeilhagel lands on its own clock with no matter (talent_fx.gd:1722). Archer arrows throw gold, coin-like chips (talent_fx.gd:890).
backlog.after: Painted matter is gated by paint_matter. Shots shed world-space embers, frost and motes per second from _step_bullets. Erdspalter kicks dust at take-off and throws rubble at landing. A burning target carries its fire. Domes chip and fall in their own element (stone plates and dust, soul motes, ice). Pfeilhagel volleys land on the damage ticks with chips, dust and a quivering shaft. Arrows splinter back off the surface with one tip spark.

backlog.title: Every flying thing uses the one particle world: world embers, hero side matter, rig chips, gold, wreck piles
backlog.what_player_sees_now: hell_game.embers and _burst (every hero blast, boss phase and death, well and level-up) are straight-line squares with no gravity that fly through walls (hell_game.gd:2198/3174). They spawn per frame, so 144 Hz shows 2.4× as many, and the 360 cap slices them off at full alpha. Block, counter and blood-price matter uses its own gravity and never lands (story_hero.gd:552). Rig chips fly through walls. Gold coins fly into walls and lie glinting on lava (gold_loot.gd:177). Settled wreck shards never move again, ice chips never melt, and shards lie on top of pits (story_wreck.gd:772).
backlog.after: _burst and the ambient embers go to the feel particles at a rate per second through room(). Sparks fall, bounce, lie as embers and turn to soot, ambient lava embers rise buoyantly, and the Krypta gets miasma instead of embers. Blood-price drops stain. Rig chips with a known floor point land. Coins bounce off wall faces, sink into lava with a hiss (D11) and are relaunched by blasts. Wreck piles are relaunched by blasts and fronts, ice chips melt, and pieces over pits fall in.

backlog.title: No popping at the particle cap, frost always melts, cheap Gefüge blob
backlog.what_player_sees_now: At the cap the oldest particle is removed (particles.gd:1945). Mid-air chunks and drops snap to the floor, smoke vanishes in one frame, and a comet can lay its puddle mid-flight. At the frost cap the dropped melt entries stay frozen forever (particles.gd:2400). The whole _vapor list, up to 4000 entries, is rescanned every frame. The fused Gefüge blob costs about 30k distance operations and 625 draw_rect calls per frame (particles.gd:1231).
backlog.after: One scan per frame picks unprotected, nearly dead cosmetic matter, which dithers out, with a hard cap at 1.05×. Airborne matter never teleports and comets always land. smoke, steam, kick and rubble go through room(). Frost always melts, and _vapor uses due-time buckets. The Gefüge blob is baked to a texture on the 12 fps beat, with one-pass nearest-lump lookups and no str().

backlog.title: Comets land on the gameplay spot; wells swallow along the path
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Comets (gore and pool splashes) land about one frame early and 6-18 crypt px short of where gameplay hits, and clink off pillars (particles.gd:656/1905). Matter near the Singularität crosses its core and slingshots back and forth, worse at low fps (particles.gd:941). A rubble block swirls like a mote.
backlog.after: Exact ballistic height (z += vz·dt - ½g·dt²) with a touchdown back-off, so comets land at the gameplay spot at any fps. Splash particles skip wall collision while high. A swept closest-approach test swallows matter whose path crosses the core (fuse particles skipped), the speed change per step is capped, and the well force is divided by mass: dust streams in first and rubble drags.

backlog.title: Traps, gates, vents and torches move and shed matter (fire_anim flame-tip hook needs the brother)
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Spikes flip between sprites (hell_game.gd:3719). Ice traps vanish in one frame (:4377). Hölle vents and the Krypta's grave-gas vent spit straight ember squares (:3097). Portcullises pop in although the toast says 'Die Gitter fallen' (:4113). Torches and braziers are sealed loops (:3673): no sparks, no smoke, no lean from a blast, no dimming from frost or water.
backlog.after: Presentation edge timers sit on the gameplay booleans. Spikes shoot up with overshoot and grit, ice spikes burst with chips and break into frost shards, vents roar buoyant flames and smoke, and the grave vent breathes green gas. Gates drop in 0.15-0.2 s with dust and a camera kick. Torches shed embers and a thread of smoke, lean and flare or gutter from pressure fronts, and hiss and dim near frost or water, all with per-second accumulators and only in view. Lighting bowls with fire follows D7.

backlog.title: Particles are hidden by actors and props by depth
backlog.what_player_sees_now: All flying matter is drawn at z 12, above the y-sorted actors at z 10 (story_feel.gd:147/652, hell_game.gd:418). Chunks, skulls, shards and drops behind a monster, Ignaroth, a pillar, a brazier, a chest or the hero are painted over them.
backlog.after: Particles are band-drawn inside _draw_actors by floor y. Matter north of a foot is covered, matter south of it covers. High matter and the glow pass stay on top. Depends on R2, so only one instance needs banding.

backlog.title: Pushes add up, point away from the blast, scale with mass and respect walls
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Talent hits set m.k to 60 px/s away from the hero, even for blasts (hell_talents.gd:477). Meteor, Nova and Urknall move living enemies about 7 px, and an enemy between the hero and the impact is pulled into it. Every zone tick resets a running shove, and photon beam ticks stop bodies dead mid-flight (hell_game.gd:1984). A sword pushes a Glutimp and a Kettenschinder the same. Thrown bodies pass through packs. On ice, monsters keep pressing into walls, stay stuck inside newly spawned ice or gravity walls, and leap slams hop through wall cells (motion_kit.gd:155). Boss shockwaves never shove adds or gas.
backlog.after: Impulses are added and clamped at about 1000 px/s, point away from the blast centre, scale by tier (D5) and by mass ((r/r_ref)², kit bosses immovable). Ticks and beams never cancel a flight. Flung or slammed bodies knock others like bowling pins (restitution 0.4). The velocity into a blocked axis is lost, bodies are pushed out of new solids, leap paths are marched in 8 px samples, and wave fronts shove non-kit monsters once per front. Depends on R6.

backlog.title: Felled bodies keep the blow; flights skid, land and roll upright
backlog.what_player_sees_now: 13 of the 18 Hölle monsters freeze where they die, play one death row and vanish after 0.75 s (hell_monsters.gd:575/1696). The blow's momentum and the Urknall tumble are dropped. Urknall flights stop dead from 760 px/s and snap upright (talent_combat.gd:2548). Rage slam kills fly into the wall. Frostgruft dash and Golem charge wall hits are silent.
backlog.after: Corpses slide with the blow, with friction, stop at walls and turn with their tumble, then dissolve as now, with ash or ember particles carrying the velocity. Flights slow down (speed·sqrt(left/total), floor 0.25) and roll back upright to the nearest TAU. Slam kills splat on the wall and come apart away from it. Dash and charge wall hits crunch with dust, a shake and a small recoil.

backlog.title: One freeze rule on the game clock; ice thaws rim first and on a timer
backlog.what_player_sees_now: Frozen zones are never marked frozen, so lightning still charges them and fire still boils them. The Frostgruft talents freeze nothing (story_feel.gd:638-642). Glatteis lasts the puddle's whole life, even beside lava (story_elements.gd:140/371). Fire pops it back to water in one frame with 4 frost sparks. Fire on a monster's frost pool does nothing in the rules.
backlog.after: story_elements.frost_at freezes its zones through a keys filter in pool_field.freeze_near, the same in all three worlds; the Frostgruft talent layer is added to set_liquids. Ice melts rim first from the fire's side over 0.5-1 s with steam and drips (per-cell thaw times, 'thawed' events in batches). It melts by itself after ice_time, faster near heat (D4). Fire on an ice pool lays melt water.

backlog.title: The Frostgruft joins the element and body physics: pools, wading, ragdolls, contact knock, boss pushes

Snowmen's frost patches slip only the hero, inside a circle, and vanish with no melt water (frost_moves.gd:494). Boss pushes are eased knocks with distance falloff, pulls slide along walls, and cc_immune stops every forced move. Monster skid marks are in R30 (brother).

decisions.question: Should the talents' leftover pools (fire, Glatteis, blood, void after shots, novas and blinks) affect gameplay? (F24, F15, F28)
options: Look only: they show, ring and wet soles, but never hurt or trip anyone
Gameplay for a named short list only (Feuerball blast fire, lava, Phönix trail, Frostsprung), laid by talent_combat on the host clock and sparing the caster
Keep as now (random length, hurts the caster, comes from drawing code)
decisions.recommendation: Look only in Phase 1, because it fixes the self-burn bug and keeps footprints deterministic. Then add the short gameplay list as its own step, where a talent's text promises a ground effect.

decisions.question: Should matter meeting matter change gameplay? This reverses the 2026-10-30 'visible only' decision (F12, F15).
options: Yes, on the host clock with residue excluded: water on fire puts it out, poison gas over lava or fire ignites, poison on lava explodes, steam over ice condenses
No: only fix the picture so it never contradicts the rules (fire stays visible, crust only where it is really crusted)
Partly: only fire plus poison becomes real; water on fire stays visual
decisions.recommendation: Do the picture fix first (R9, no rule change). Then option 1, because it is what 'every effect is the physics of its element' means. It needs one balance check in Krypta and Hölle.

decisions.question: How should the Krypta's Moder behave in gameplay? (F48)
options: Cold poison sludge: poison on it does nothing, water only ripples, debris sinks without glow
Keep the lava rules (poison explodes, water boils) under the green look
Sludge whose miasma a fire spell ignites into a flash

decisions.question: How long should Glatteis last in the story worlds, and which liquids can frost freeze? (F17, F18)

Lasts the pool's whole life as now; frost freezes water, blood and poison
Melts only when fire touches it

decisions.question: How hard should talent blasts and shockwaves push living enemies? (F37, F44, F40)
options: Fix direction and make pushes add up now; ultimate-sized pushes only on the final blow; mass by body size normalized to the median mob so typical mobs are unchanged
Full pushes by tier on every hit (enemies get thrown out of the Meteor crater and Singularität fields)
Fix the direction only and keep 60 px/s

decisions.question: Should enemy blasts and boss slams break crates, urns, seals and skull heaps? (F49)

decisions.question: Should a fire spell light an unlit puzzle fire bowl? (F56)

No: the puzzles stay E-only; fire only makes the flame flare
decisions.recommendation: Yes, direct hit only, so a single blast cannot light a whole puzzle out of order.

decisions.question: What should the world do during the 1.8 s after the hero dies? (F42)
options: Everything keeps moving with damage off
A uniform slow motion for everything, particles included
Everything freezes, particles included

Spat back onto the rim
Lost

findings.title: Hero skills/attacks run a second, disconnected particle world: embers and frost lie on top of Hölle lava, gas and the ice slab
findings.now: The story worlds run two separate Particles instances. One is story_skill_fx.particles, which attack_fx also uses (story_hero.gd:156): hero shot impacts, fireball/fist bursts, Photoneneis. The other is feel.feedback.particles: talents, monsters, element reactions and boss pools. Only the feel instance gets set_sink (story_feel.gd:799), set_liquids (:642) and the sound sink (story_sound.gd:709). What the player sees: a hero fireball or fire-mage hit over lava leaves glowing embers, a soot stain and smoke ON the lava, because embers() has no sink check and the kit has no sink cells. Frost fist frost and rime grow over lava. The kit's ground layer is z 5 like the feel's but is created later (hell_game.gd:369 vs :423/:714), so its floor marks are drawn over the lava pools, the gas clouds, the Frostgruft ice slab and the hero shadow. A monster blow/kick or the Singularität well moves the world's debris while the hero's own debris and embers next to it lie still. The hero's matter makes no landing sounds. Each instance has its own 600-particle budget.
findings.should: One matter world: hero embers that land in lava hiss out, the hero's marks lie under the liquid surfaces, every blast lifts every loose pixel, wells swallow all matter, one budget and one sound path.
findings.proposal: As proposed: point skill_fx.particles, skill_fx.skill.particles and attack.particles at g.feel.feedback.particles when g.feel != null. Add a `shared` flag to StorySkillFx. With it set, skip particles.update, the draw_stains/draw_particles/particles.draw_glow calls, and particles.clear()/set_walkable in _set_floor, but keep fx.clear()/fx.set_walkable. Two 600 budgets become one, so raise max_particles (e.g. 900) or give hero effects room(weight). Without a feel, copy the sink cells and liquids into the kit instance. Add sinks() skips to embers(), frost(), stain() and scatter().
findings.check: Confirmed. StorySkillFx creates its own `Particles.new()` (story_skill_fx.gd:47), and StoryHero points attack.particles at it (story_hero.gd:156). Only feel.feedback.particles gets set_sink (story_feel.gd:799), set_liquids (:642) and the sound sink (story_sound.gd:709). So kit kicks do not ripple the pools either, because their _liquids is empty. embers() (particles.gd:493), frost(), stain() and scatter() have no sinks() check. The kit has no sink cells at all, so its rime_grow and glut also land on lava. The kit's ground layer (z5) is added after the feel's (hell_game.gd:369 vs :423/:714), so its draw_stains draws over the feel's pools, gas, ice slab and hero shadow. Wells, kick and blow on one instance never touch the other. All three themes have a feel, so this happens in every story world. The feel already shares the kit's FxSprites (story_feel.gd:479 feedback.fx = kit.fx), so sharing the particles the other way is consistent and feasible. Units match: both scales are hero_scale/2 with 32 px cells.

findings.title: All matter makes contact like a rubber ball: drops bounce and slide, fire and smoke bounce off walls, shards skate across lava
findings.now: _move has one contact rule for every mode. A wall hit keeps 40 % of the speed reflected (wall_bounce) and all of the tangential speed. A floor hit faster than 70 px/s bounces at 0.35 and keeps 60 % sliding under ground friction. So liquid drops (drop mode from drops(), splat_burst blood, Gefüge water/poison bits) hop and roll 5-10 px like beads before they lie down. Flames pushed by fire_burst (up to 2.4×radius px/s) and smoke bounce back off walls. Sinking is only tested once a particle is at rest (_settle :1971/:1995), so ice shards, rubble, rolling skulls and glowing glut pixels bounce and skate across Hölle lava and only vanish where they stop. Water or blood drops falling into lava vanish without a hiss (only frost steams there). kick() erases wet pixels with no spray (:1639) and throws pool/stain pixels as hard 'debris' chips (:1648).
findings.should: Each material makes contact in its own way. A drop splats on first contact: a short streak along its flight, a 1-2 px crown when fast, a ripple and no paint if it lands in a pool. On a wall a drop paints the wall face or runs to its foot. Flames and smoke lose their speed into the wall and creep along it. Ice clinks and rubble thuds. Touching lava at z<=0 sinks the matter at once: a hiss for water, ice and frost, a small plop for heavy debris.
findings.proposal: As proposed, with one change: do not reuse `particle.landed` for drops or wall sticks. update() sends landed particles to _land_splash, which spawns a comet crown and reads splash/land_ref. Use a separate flag (e.g. `stuck`) that update() handles by calling the new _land_drop() or wall_splat() and then removing the particle. Add the sinks() check (plop/steam) to the skull branch of _settle. Per-mode contact data (wall: bounce|slide|stick, floor: bounce|splat) in vfx_particles.json is a sound way to do it. Give flame/smoke/mote wall 'slide' with a low wall_keep.
findings.check: Confirmed in _move (particles.gd:1869-1881, 1909-1928). Every non-free particle reflects off walls at wall_bounce 0.4 on one axis and keeps the other axis. That includes flames, smoke and motes, since settle does not matter there. A floor hit below -70 px/s bounces at 0.35 with velocity×0.6. Drops (drop mode, gravity 1, lift 50-140, speed 60-160, drag 2) hop and then slide about v/11 s ≈ 5 px before settling. sinks() is only tested in _settle (:1971, :1995), and only frost steams there. Also missed: the skull branch of _settle (:1961-1969) returns before any sinks() check, so rolling skulls lie on Hölle lava for good. kick() drops _wet pixels silently (:1639) and throws pool/stain pixels as 'debris' (:1648).

findings.title: No air drag on height and weightless matter cannot rise: flakes speed up, smoke and embers shoot up forever, motes 'rise' across the floor
findings.element: smoke, steam, fire, snow, soul/holy motes
findings.now: Drag only acts on the floor-plane velocity (:1940). vz has gravity but no air resistance, and weightless modes cannot move vertically at all: emit sets vz=0 when gravity==0 (:217), and _move integrates z only when gravity != 0. Result: snow flakes (flake, gravity 0.08) speed up all the way down (0 to about 60 px/s) instead of drifting at a steady rate. Smoke, steam (-0.06) and embers (-0.12) accelerate upwards for their whole life as rigid, constant-size columns of about 90-100 crypt px, and cooled embers never sink. Motes 'rise' by moving their floor point north: motes() :1394 Vector2(0,-rise), holy() :1497 -10..-24 px/s, a -y bias in smoke/steam. So they bounce off the foot of north walls at 40 % and drift into other cells. A flame's bloom also stays its first white-yellow at full strength while its pixel cools down the ramp (draw_glow :2214 uses particle.color, fade=false), then pops off.
findings.should: Buoyant matter reaches a terminal rise speed while it slows and widens: smoke spreads, steam thins. Embers rise, then drift down as they cool. Flakes fall slowly at a steady speed. Motes rise in height, not across the floor. A flame's glow cools and fades with the flame.
findings.proposal: As proposed (vz = (vz - g·dt)·exp(-air·dt), terminal speed g/air), with these corrections. steam() emits mode 'smoke', so 'steam air 2' needs a new 'steam' mode or a per-particle air override set in steam(). Keep air 0 for every mode comet() uses (drop, glut, shard, debris, mote), because comet() solves lift for a drag-free arc. Embers mode is not settle, so after the gravity flip a cooled ember should fall and fade (or call _cool for a soot pixel at z<=0). In draw_glow, use the ramp colour by age and alpha×(1-age) for ramp particles.
findings.check: Confirmed. Drag only scales vel (particles.gd:1940). vz has no air term. emit sets vz=0 when gravity==0 (:217), and z is only integrated when gravity != 0 (:1904). Flakes: g = 0.08×620 = 49.6 px/s² from flake_height 14-40 px, so they reach 37-63 px/s at landing. Smoke (and steam, which emits mode 'smoke') rises at -0.06×620 and embers at -0.12×620, accelerating for their whole life. Smoke size is a constant 4 px. motes() (:1394) and holy() (:1497) move the floor point north (-y). draw_glow (:2214) uses particle.color with fade=false for flames (mode flame fade false), so the bloom stays the ramp's first colour at full alpha while draw_particles cools the flame.

findings.title: Particles are never hidden by actors or props: debris behind a monster, pillar or hero is drawn in front of it
findings.now: All flying particles of both instances are drawn in one pass, on layers at z 12 (story_feel.gd:147 'over', story_hero.gd:166). That is above the y-sorted actors/props layer (hell_game.gd:418 z 10, sorted at :3773). Chunks, skulls, shards, sparks and blood drops that fly or roll behind a monster, Ignaroth, a pillar, a brazier, a chest or the hero (north of its feet) are painted over it, so the 2.5D depth is lost.
findings.should: A particle whose floor point lies north of an actor's foot is covered by the actor; one south of the foot covers the actor.
findings.proposal: As proposed. Sort by pos.y (floor point, ×scale for world y), and band-draw inside _draw_actors with draw_set_transform(Vector2.ZERO, 0, Vector2.ONE*feel.scale). Keep z>~40 px matter and the glow pass in the over/glow layers. If #0 is not done, both instances need banding.
findings.check: Confirmed. Both particle passes draw on layers at z12 (story_feel.gd:147 'over', story_hero.gd:166). The y-sorted actors/props/mobs/hero layer is z10 (hell_game.gd:418, sort :3773). So every flying chunk, skull, shard or drop is painted over any monster, prop or hero, whatever its floor y. The proposal is feasible: _draw_actors already iterates a y-sorted list, particles carry a floor point (pos, crypt units ×scale = world y), and draw_set_transform with the feel scale is already used in story_feel. Sorting ≤600 indices per frame is cheap.

findings.title: Void wells miss their own core: fast matter jumps across it and slingshots back and forth, worse at low fps
findings.now: _step_wells only swallows a particle whose current position is inside the core (d <= core), then adds acceleration (pull+swirl)×near, with near up to 6, by explicit Euler. The move happens later in _move. Near the Singularität (core = 0.12 r, about 7 crypt px; pull 260 / swirl 180, so 600-1900 px/s²) matter reaches 250-600 px/s. That is 5-10 px per frame at 60 fps and 12-30 px at the 0.05 dt clamp (hell_game.gd:2490). So particles cross the core without being taken, get pulled back and ping-pong through the middle. All matter is pulled equally: a 6 px rubble block or a skull swirls like a mote; only Gefüge divides by its units.
findings.should: Like a drain: matter spirals in, turning faster as it nears, and vanishes the moment its path crosses the core. Light dust and motes stream in first; heavy rubble drags along the floor.
findings.proposal: Add the swept closest-approach core test, but skip `fuse` particles. The core holds Gefüge matter (the `own` branch) and must never swallow it. Add modes.*.mass and divide the well force by it. Prefer keeping the acceleration model with a per-step cap on the speed change, rather than a velocity-target rewrite of every well. A velocity target also changes the boss vortex, the pool void wells, swallow, rift and the Blizzard wind (core 1, suck=false), so if you adopt it, tune it per well.
findings.check: Confirmed. _step_wells (particles.gd:919-950) removes a particle only if its current position is within the core, before _move advances it. It adds (pull·inward + swirl·tangent)·near·dt with near up to 6, and nothing tests the swept path. The Singularität uses pull 260, swirl 180 and core = 0.12·r·s (talent_fx.gd:500). Light-drag motes can reach several hundred px/s, so at the 0.05 dt clamp (hell_game.gd:2490) a step is longer than the core's diameter. At a steady 60 fps the core catches most radial passes, so the effect is mainly at low fps. Mass: only Gefüge divides by n. Rock, skull and debris get the same acceleration as motes.

findings.title: Blasts and wells act through walls: kick, blow, the wells' pull and _suck have no occlusion
findings.element: fire blasts, shockwaves, void, frost nova
findings.now: kick() lifts every loose or stain pixel in its reach square; only the pixel's own cell is tested (:1645). blow() pushes every particle and floor pixel in its band (:1673-1727). _step_wells pulls every particle within r (:930-950), and _suck lifts floor pixels within 0.8 r (:1272-1292). None of them checks walls in between. A fireball or shockwave against a corridor wall makes debris and embers in the next room jump outward on their own. A Singularität next to a wall drags loose pixels from behind the wall to its foot, where they pile up. Frost novas (frost_fx.gd:233) and hell_monsters blows (:3126) shove matter in the neighbouring corridor. Gas is stopped by walls, so the elements disagree.
findings.should: A blast's pressure and a well's pull only reach matter they can see; matter behind a wall stays put.
findings.proposal: Add _sees(origin, point), a DDA over the 32 px _walkable grid that stops at the first solid cell. In kick, blow and _suck, cache cell -> visible per call (at most about (2r/32)² cells) and skip pixels and particles in hidden cells. In _step_wells, cache visibility per well for 0.1 s. Apply the same filter before calling pool_paint ripple_near in kick's _liquids loop.
findings.check: Confirmed. kick() only tests solid() of each pixel's own cell (particles.gd:1645). blow() pushes every particle, ember and loose pixel in the band (:1673-1727). _step_wells (:930-950) and _suck (:1272-1292) have no line-of-sight test either. Callers include frost_fx.gd:233 P.blow and hell_monsters.gd:3126 P.blow. Story cells are 96 world px = 64 crypt px, so a one-tile wall is thinner than typical kick and blow radii, and matter in the next corridor visibly jumps. The DDA over the 32 px _walkable grid, cached per cell per call, is cheap and feasible.

findings.title: Eviction at the cap teleports airborne debris to the floor and pops cosmetics; most emitters bypass room(); frost at its cap never melts
findings.now: At max_particles every emit() calls _evict(). It removes the oldest particle and, if that is debris, settles it at its floor point: mid-air chunks, drops and shards snap onto the floor under them, and smoke and motes vanish in one frame. Only Gefüge is protected. Comets, documented as 'never skipped', are not: an evicted comet with land_ref lays its puddle at its mid-flight floor point (:1990). The cap is easy to hit because most emitters skip room(): smoke() (:1574) fed by every floor ember (_burn_embers :2384, up to 500 embers), steam(), kick() (up to 140 per blast), rubble(), holy(), shadow(), _suck, plus 40 direct emit/burst calls in feedback.gd and 32 in hell_monsters.gd. Frost has the same pattern: at frost.max, _freeze drops the oldest melt/vapor entry (:2400, :2405), and those pixels stay frozen forever. The whole _vapor list (up to 4000 entries) is rescanned every frame (:2438).
findings.should: At the cap, nearly dead cosmetic matter fades out by the dither instead of popping. Airborne matter never teleports, comets always land, and frost always melts.
findings.proposal: As proposed for which particles to protect: fuse, splash, land_ref and airborne settle particles (z>1). Do not run a full least-life scan inside every emit at the cap. kick() alone can call emit 140 times in one frame, which would make that O(n²). Instead, find candidates once per frame in update(), or scan from the oldest for the first unprotected non-settle particle. Set its life to min(life, 0.1), tag it 'evicting' so later calls skip it, and pop only above a 1.05× hard cap. Route smoke, steam, kick and rubble through room(). At the frost cap, melt the dropped entry at once. Put _vapor into due-time buckets.
findings.check: Confirmed. _evict (particles.gd:1945) removes the oldest non-fuse particle and _settle()s it when it is settle. _settle ignores z, so airborne debris, drops and shards are painted at their floor point. A comet with land_ref calls drop_landed at its mid-flight point (:1989). Cosmetic particles pop. smoke(), steam(), kick() (own limit 140), rubble(), holy(), shadow() and _suck skip room(). _burn_embers spawns smoke per ember (:2384, up to 500 embers). Direct emit/burst calls: about 35 in feedback.gd and 30 in hell_monsters.gd. Frost at its cap: _freeze advances _frost_head or pop_front()s _vapor (:2400, :2405) without melting, and the pixel stays in _frozen for good. _melt rescans the whole _vapor array every frame (:2436-2450).

findings.title: Gefüge blob drawing is an O(pixels × lumps × 2) GDScript loop every frame
findings.now: _draw_fused redraws every blob pixel by pixel each frame. For each of up to (2·ceil(r)+5)² art pixels (625 for a full 40 px blob) it loops over all lumps (fuse.lumps 24) to find the nearest one. It loops again for the nearest lump of another element, calling str() on every lump, and calls off.angle() and sin() per pixel. findings.title: Wall hits bounce off empty air up to v·dt short of the wall; corners are cut; matter born in a wall passes through it

A particle spawned inside a wall (free, :1865) flies through it until it leaves, possibly on the far side.

findings.proposal: On solid(next), compute the crossed cell boundary per axis (floor(next/32)*32 or +32), clamp to the boundary minus 0.5 px, then reflect. If next is solid but both single-axis moves are open (a corner), reflect on the axis with the smaller penetration. Sub-step moves longer than 16 px (wells, comets). findings.title: Comets land early and short by about v·dt (Euler vs analytic arc) and clink off walls away from the gameplay spot
findings.now: comet() solves lift with the continuous formula (0.5 g t² - h)/t. _move integrates height with semi-implicit Euler (vz -= g·dt, then z += vz·dt, :1905-1906), which loses 0.5·g·t·dt of height. The blob touches down about 0.9 frame early and about v·dt short: for a 400 px/s comet that is 6 crypt px (9 world px) at 60 fps and 18 crypt px at the clamp, so the splash misses the spot where gameplay hits. Its floor path also collides with walls (p.free=false, :663): a comet whose straight line clips a pillar or wall cell bounces off at 40 % and splashes somewhere else.

findings.proposal: As proposed: z += vz·dt - 0.5·g·dt²; vz -= g·dt, with the touchdown back-off pos -= vel·(z/vz). This is exact only with no air drag, so if #2 adds `air`, it must stay 0 for the comet modes, or comets need their own drag-free branch. For particles with `splash`, skip wall collision while z > ~24 px.

For T=0.5 s, h=10 that is 2.6 px at 60 fps, so the comet lands about 0.9 frame early and about 0.9·v·dt short: about 6 crypt px for 400 px/s, and about 18 px at the 0.05 clamp. findings.title: Pool reactions are only drawn and contradict the rules: fire that looks put out keeps burning, crust that looks safe still burns, poison hisses instead of exploding
findings.element: fire, lava, water, blood, poison, ice
findings.now: _react/_react_pair (1639) and _react_hot (1661) apply the vfx_pools.json reactions by style. poison, blood and water are all style 'liquid'. So 'liquid+fire' hides the fire cells (field.hide) and puffs steam. 'liquid+lava', 'ice+lava' and the hot lava tiles get a dark crust painted on. All of this is drawing only. The rules read PoolField.materials_at plus ElementRules.top (lava > fire > ice > poison > void > water > blood). So a blood or water pool over burning ground shows bare blood while the hero keeps burning. The fire also stays invisible after the blood dries, because hide is only cleared when the fire's own cells end. A poison pool touching fire shows a steam hiss (poison 'putting out' fire), yet the rules would make it explode; fire_at only runs when a fire attack lands, never when pools meet. Draw crust only where story_elements.crusted(at) is true: pass a Callable in like `hot`, or let the snapshot's 'cr' (_crust_pool) be the only source. findings.title: Ignited poison gas does not burn: it fades green from its centroid and gets blown outward by its own blast

But timings() (116-122) counts its cells' births from the zone's start, with spread_time 0.35 s. So by the time it is laid, about 90% of the cells are already born. The potion shatters, nothing lies there for a third of a second, then the full pool appears in one frame, and the splash and crown (_show_pool 249) only fire at that moment. The other direction: when a void mouth shortens a puddle (story_elements 213-215 / 277-279 set z.T = t + drain), sync_zone ignores the new length of a known pool. The pool stays full while its motes stream away, then vanishes rim first in 0.35 s once the zone drops (end_missing → finish).
findings.should: Matter lands and runs out from the moment of impact. A drained pool shrinks toward the mouth while it drains.
findings.proposal: For a threaded job, pass start' = max(start, job.commit) into timings() inside add(). commit is a pure function of the cell count, so every machine still gets the same result, and the pool spreads after it shows instead of popping in. In PoolPaint.sync, when sync_zone returns a key that is still in pool_field._shaping and the zone is fresh, play the crown and drops at once from the zone's x, y, dx, dy and r. In sync_zone, for a known key compare start+L with pool.end. If it is shorter, call a new PoolField.retime(key, now, new_end, toward) that sets each cell's until between now and new_end by its distance from `toward` (the mouth, which void_at passes), so the far rim goes first.
findings.check: Confirmed. add() starts a WorkerThreadPool job for >= thread_cells (600) cells with commit = _now + commit_delay. The worker computes timings(cells, start, end, ...) with the zone's original start and spread_time 0.35 s. _show_pool fires (and splashes) only on 'laid' at commit, and the cells born before then all show at once. A poison potion is radius 72 × leveling scale 2.4 at art 3, roughly 7,800 cells by cells_for, so commit is about 0.5 s. That is longer than the whole spread, so the full pool pops in, even worse than the finding says. sync_zone returns early for a known key, so the shorter z.T a void drain sets is ignored until the zone drops and end_missing → finish runs it off rim first in 0.35 s. hell_monsters pool_entries passes L = z.T. The proposal is feasible and deterministic, because commit depends only on the field clock and the cell count. Capture start' before creating the task.

findings.title: Frostgruft pools sit outside the element physics: no reactions, monsters never slide on move ice, potions are plain circles
findings.now: The Frostgruft has no monster runtime. update() returns before contacts and charges (183-185), _puddles finds nothing, talent_pool makes no pool (hell_talents.gd 402-403), and thrown potions stay story_items circles (story_items.gd 720 only zones them when monsters exist). The snowmen's frost_patch ice pools (frost_moves.gd 494-500) slip only the hero, inside a circle, and are drawn as frost_fx's slab (frost_fx.gd 285-330). Monsters never slide on them, the hero's fire does not melt them, and they vanish cell by cell with no melt water. In Krypta and Hölle the same ice is a PoolField pool: everyone slides, it cracks and it leaves melt water.
findings.should: The same matter has the same physics in all three worlds.
findings.proposal: Make the Frostgruft's pool layer (g._pool_layer() = talents.fx.pools) the rules' truth there too. frost_moves._pool also syncs its zone into that layer as {k:'pool', st:'ice', source:'frost_moves'}. ElementExposure (already used by _step_mob_medium) then makes monsters slide, and pool_paint draws it with cracks and melt water. Drop frost_fx's slab for move pools and keep it for the ice floor tiles. Route hero_pool into the same layer when monsters is null. With reactions working on field pools (see the contact-reaction finding), story_elements no longer needs g.monsters for pools.
findings.check: Confirmed. In story_elements.update, `if g.monsters == null: return` skips contacts and charges. hell_talents.talent_pool and story_items.hero_pool create zones only when monsters exist. frost_moves._pool zones are circles that only call HeroFx.apply(g,'slip') on the hero (frost_moves 494-497). frost_fx's slab draws them, and fire never reaches them. Frostgruft mobs do run exposure().step through _step_mob_medium (hell_game 2920), and g._pool_layer() resolves to talents.fx.pools there. So syncing the move pools into that layer as PoolField 'ice' pools would let monsters slide. The proposal is feasible, if large. frost_moves.gd and frost_fx.gd are not on the brother's list.

findings.title: Overlapping pools hide each other by spawn order, not by which one acts, and liquids never mix
findings.now: draw() paints each material's texture in _fields insertion order: the material that first appeared in the room is at the bottom. Water and blood are opaque, so whichever came later covers the other completely, outline included. The rules pick by priority (ElementRules.top). A water puddle laid over poison shows clean water while the hero is being poisoned. Blood dropped into water shows a red sheet with a hard outline on blue instead of colouring the water. liquid_at and wet_at (1765) also answer by insertion order.
findings.should: The material that acts is the one you see. Miscible liquids tint each other: blood clouds into water, poison turns it green and fuming. Immiscible ones (lava, ice) clearly sit over or under.
findings.proposal: Sort the draw loop and liquid_at by ElementRules priority, reversed, so the material that counts is drawn last (lava and fire on top, blood at the bottom); cache the order when _fields' keys change. Add drawing-only mix rules to vfx_pools.json reactions, keyed by material: 'water+blood' → a_to 'bloodwater', 'water+poison' → a_to 'toxicwater'. Give them their own ramps: bloodwater is the water ramp lerped 40% toward blood; toxicwater keeps the miasma veil and fumes. _react_pair already turns overlap cells into a drawing-only material.
findings.check: Confirmed. PoolPaint.draw loops `for mat in _fields` in insertion order. _fields entries are created on first use by _field() and erased when they empty, so the order depends on spawn history. Water and blood are opaque (comment at pool_paint 860; only poison has the miasma veil). liquid_at (1765) also returns the first material in insertion order. Rules priority is lava > fire > ice > poison > void > water > blood, so water drawn over poison hides the material that is acting. Same-style pairs have no reaction key: the lookup is _style(a)+'+'+_style(b), and 'liquid+liquid' does not exist, so liquids never mix. Sorting the draw order by reversed priority is cheap. The mix rules need _react to also look up material-keyed rules, which is feasible.

findings.title: Gas parting depends on the frame rate, and shots never cut through gas in the story worlds
findings.now: part() adds a velocity kick (speed*k*0.2) and moves each puff k*0.6 px per call, with no dt. hell_game._step_gas (3342-3344) calls it once per frame for the hero and for every monster. At 144 fps the hero parts gas 2.4x harder than at 60 fps. ElementExposure breathes the ring around his feet (gas_around, 57 px) and the vision reads extent(), so his poison dose and his view range depend on the frame rate. cut() (243, also per call with no dt) is only called by the old dungeon_view.gd (855). Arrows, fireballs and monster shots fly through clouds in all three story worlds without leaving a lane.
findings.should: Parting is a force per second, the same at any frame rate. Every shot cuts a lane through the gas that closes again behind it.
findings.proposal: Change the signatures to part(at, radius, dt) and cut(at, dir, width, dt), and scale both the velocity term and the position nudge by dt*60 (or rewrite them as speed*k*12*dt). In hell_game._step_gas, call gas.cut(s.p, s.v, 6*PIXEL_WORLD/2, dt) for each eshot and each talents.bullets entry (b.pos, b.velocity) that lies inside a cloud's bounds. Scale the monsters' part radius with m.r instead of the flat 18.
findings.check: Confirmed. GasField.part adds speed*k*0.2 to velocity and k*0.6 px to position per call, with no dt. hell_game._process → _update → _update_embers → _step_gas calls it once per rendered frame for the hero and every monster, with variable dt and no fixed-step accumulator. Nothing in project.godot caps the frame rate. So at 144 fps the parting is about 2.4x stronger, which changes what ElementExposure.gas_around reads (the hero's dose) and the vision extent. gas.cut is called only by the obsolete dungeon_view.gd 855. The story worlds' eshots ({p, v}) and hell_talents bullets ({pos, velocity}) never cut lanes. The proposal (dt-scaled part and cut, cut calls in _step_gas, part radius from m.r) fits the existing data shapes.

findings.title: Talent projectiles never check the end of their step, so at 60 fps they fly through every wall
findings.element: all talent projectiles (Feuerball, Infernospeer, Frostlanze, Splittersalve, Leerengeschoss/-lanze, all archer arrows, Wurfmesser, necro bolts)
findings.now: _step_bullets (line 543) relies only on talent_blocked(from, b.pos, 3.0). talent_blocked samples i in range(1, steps) with steps = max(1, ceil(dist/12)), so it never tests the end point. When a frame's step is under 12 px the loop does not run at all: at 440 px/s that is any frame rate of 37 fps or more, at 560 px/s for arrows 47 fps or more. At 60 fps a talent shot never meets a wall. It turns invisible inside the wall (PixelPaint.clip), comes out in the next room and hits monsters behind the wall. talent_fx._settle_shots works out the 'impact' from the shot vanishing, so the boom/shatter and the residue happen wherever its 1.6 s life ends, about 700 px away, often in mid-air.
findings.should: A shot stops at the first wall on the segment it sweeps. It bursts at the contact point on the wall face, and its sparks/shards bounce off the wall normal.
findings.proposal: Keep talent_blocked unchanged for the melee line-of-sight check. Give _step_bullets its own sweep: sample range(1, steps+1) every 6 px or less, including the end point. On the first blocked sample, bisect about 6 times to get the contact point, and take the normal with the same side probes story_feel.wall_hit uses (story_feel.gd:258-290). For the blocked test use story_feel.blocked (cell plus solid_grid grown 50 px), the same test basic shots use, or g.box_blocked; pick one and use it everywhere. Put the shot at the contact point and call g.feel.wall_hit(from, b.pos, style, 1) with the existing wall-style names: {fireball/infernospear:'fire', frost_lance:'frost', arcane:'void', arrow:'arrow', blade:'metal'}. 'ice' is not a valid wall style (SHOT_WALL_STYLES/ENEMY_WALL_STYLES use 'frost'). Expose {at, normal, talent, style} through a shot_ends list in tc.snapshot so talent_fx._impact uses the real contact instead of the guess at talent_fx.gd:777.
findings.check: Confirmed. talent_blocked (hell_talents.gd:457-461) samples range(1, steps) with steps=max(1,ceil(d/12)), so the end point is never tested and nothing is tested when the step is under 12 px. Shot speeds are 440 px/s, and 560 px/s for arrows (talent_combat.gd:366). hell_game._process passes a variable dt (min(delta, 0.05)), so at 60 fps a step is 7-9 px and is never checked. The enemy loop in _step_bullets has no line-of-sight check, so shots hit monsters behind walls. _settle_shots/_impact fire wherever the 1.6 s life runs out (about 704 px away), and the residue is left there too.

findings.title: Residue pools are made by the drawing code, yet they hurt and trip the hero and monsters
findings.element: fire, ice, poison, blood, void, lava residue
findings.now: _leave (959) creates residue pools on the client only. They come from shots _settle_shots guesses have vanished (also on walls and at expiry, where bullet_hit put no element), from every nova's _burst_physics and from blinks, and each gets a random length from _h(_local_id()). They are synced as source 'talent_residue' into the same pool layer whose materials_at (pool_field.gd:298, no source filter) feeds ElementExposure for the hero and the monsters (story_exposure_host.gd:45; the hero has no tags and is exempt only from the void). Results: a Feuerball into a nearby wall leaves fire that burns the Feuermagier ('im Feuer verbrannt'). Every Wirbelsturm/Blutiger Schrei (berserk element = blood) leaves a blood slick under the berserker's feet even with no hit (slide, grip 0.35, slip). A Frostlanze on a wall leaves Glatteis (grip 0.015). A void shot that fizzles leaves a pool that hurts, pulls and silences. Damage depends on draw passes and a local counter.
findings.should: Pools that hurt are placed deterministically by gameplay, where gameplay put the element, and spare the caster like his other talent puddles. The picture only follows them.
findings.proposal: (a) does not work as described. PoolField merges the cells of one material from all pools into a single _cells[mat] map (_lay, pool_field.gd:525-545), and cells carry no source, so materials_at cannot skip a source. Either keep drawn residue out of the gameplay layer (give talent_fx its own visual-only PoolPaint for 'talent_residue'), or tag cells from visual sources so _lay never merges them with gameplay cells and have materials_at/covers/liquid_at skip the tagged cells. (b) The claim that talent_pool spares the hero is wrong. Its friend flag only skips the hell_monsters puddle zone hit (hell_monsters.gd:1606). The pool still acts on the hero through ElementExposure (pools_under), and talent_pool does nothing in the Frostgruft (g.monsters == null). To spare the caster, pass the owner into pool_entries, make StoryExposureHost.pools_under build the hero's list from pool_field.pools_at(at) without the hero's own or friend pools, and lay Frostgruft talent pools into the fallback layer with owner set. Then create residue that should act (Feuerball explosion, lava, Phönix trail, Frostsprung) from talent_combat events, with times from talents.json.
findings.check: Confirmed. _leave (talent_fx.gd:959) creates residue from the drawing code with times from _h(_local_id()). draw_ground syncs it as 'talent_residue' (line 342) into fx.pools, which is g.pools in Krypta and Hölle and the fallback layer that _pool_layer returns in the Frostgruft. StoryExposureHost.pools_under → materials_at has no source or owner filter, so ElementExposure.step acts on the hero: the fire medium hurts and burns him ('im Feuer verbrannt'), ice gives grip 0.015, blood slips. These cases are all real: berserk novas (element blood) leave a blood pool at the hero's own position through _burst_physics, the Phönixschritt trail lays fire pools all the way to his landing spot, and a Frostsprung lands him on ice. One detail: the 'Feuerball into a nearby wall' example cannot happen at 60 fps today because of #0. It becomes real once #0 is fixed.

findings.title: Giftwolke gas comes back whole right after it explodes or is swallowed, and can be set off again
findings.element: poison gas (trapper_7 Giftwolke, Giftköder trap clouds)

For gameplay, when story_elements ignites or eats a 'talent:<id>' cloud, call talents.tc end_zone(id) (set time to 0) so the poison ticks stop together with the gas.

findings.title: The necromancer's poison and soul zones are see-through circles and sprite sheets, not gas or pools

findings.element: fire (Feuerball, Infernospeer, pyro basic), ice (Frostlanze mist), void (core motes)
