findings.title: Impact drops, motes, shards, feathers and the Glutkette's flames are painted next to their particle twins
findings.element: poison, blood, curse/soul motes, block shards, fire
findings.now: TalentPixels.impact 'drop' (1311-1327) and 'mote' (1295-1309) are not gated by paint_matter, although _impact/_observe also throw particles.drops/motes for the same hit. Giftpfeil, Dornenfalle, the curse/soul bolts and companion bleeds show two sets: painted ones that vanish mid-arc and real ones that splat. In _extra_event: block_break paints 8 falling shards on top of _matter's 8 (1997), pet_strike paints 5 blood drops on top of _matter's 6 (2011), meteor_fall paints an ember streak only (1925), dive paints feather cells only (1968), and the phoenix's ember dots are painted (1829). The Glutkette's burn is the hero rage-aura painter (TalentPixels.flames, 1022) placed at the fixed hit point (_burning at `hit`, 2317), while _damage_enemy knocks the target 60 px away, so the flames hang where it was.
findings.should: One set of matter, living in the particles; a burning target carries its fire with it.
findings.proposal: Gate those loops with TalentPixels.paint_matter. meteor_fall: _defer ember emits along the rock's path (same formula as 1924) every 0.05 s. dive: particles.emit 'debris' feathers with high drag and low gravity. Glutkette: drop the painted _burning while particles exist; instead emit particles.flames at the target every 0.08 s for chain.burn s (put enemy ids into the chain points and resolve them via enemy_at), or rely on the monster's own fire_t look.
findings.check: Confirmed. TalentPixels.impact's 'mote' and 'drop' branches have no paint_matter gate, while _impact/_matter throw particles.drops/motes for the same hit. block_break paints 8 shards on top of _matter's 8, and pet_strike paints 5 drops on top of _matter's 6. meteor_fall (an 8-cell ember streak), dive (beast cells) and the phoenix ember dots are painted only. The Glutkette's _burning draws TalentPixels.flames (the rage-aura painter, not gated) at the fixed `hit` point. One detail is overstated: m.k = dir*60 is a decaying push velocity, not a 60 px shove, so the knockback alone moves the target only about 10-20 px. The painted flames still drift off the target because it keeps walking during the 0.6 s burn.

findings.title: The hero kit and attacks use a second particle world that wells, blasts, pools and gas never touch
findings.element: hero kit skills and basic-attack element bursts
findings.now: StorySkillFx creates its own Particles.new(), and story_hero.gd:156 points attack_fx at it. Talents, gore, pools, mage bolts and enemy blasts use g.feel.feedback.particles (hell_talents.gd:83, hell_monsters._blow_front). The crypt shares one instance (dungeon_view.gd:418). In the story worlds, whirl dust, chain-lightning sparks, kit fireball embers, frost shards and the attacks' element bursts are not pulled by the Singularität or void-pool wells, not shoved by Raumsprung or enemy blasts (P.blow), and do not land in pools or touch gas (set_liquids is set only on the feedback particles, story_feel.gd:640-643). They also have their own cap and draw order.
findings.should: All matter lives in one physical world.
findings.proposal: In story_hero.gd, when g.feel exists, set skill_fx.particles, skill_fx.skill.particles and attack.particles to g.feel.feedback.particles. Add an owns_particles flag to StorySkillFx so that update, _set_floor, draw_ground, draw_over and draw_glow skip particles.update/clear/set_walkable/draw_* when the instance is shared (feedback already steps and draws it).
findings.check: Confirmed. StorySkillFx has its own `var particles := Particles.new()`, steps, clears and draws it itself (story_skill_fx.gd:140,244-274), and story_hero.gd:156 sets attack.particles to it. Talents (hell_talents.gd:83), pools, boss_fx and set_liquids (story_feel.gd:637-642) use feel.feedback.particles. So kit and attack matter never sees those wells, blows or liquids. Both instances use the same crypt scale (theme.hero_scale/2 in story_hero and story_feel), so sharing one instance is feasible with the owns_particles guard as proposed.

findings.title: Pfeilhagel: arrows fall on a free-running clock, not the damage ticks, and leave no matter
findings.now: Arrows land on `clock*1.6 + i/count*3`: each lands every 0.625 s, evenly spread, with no link to the zone's 0.5 s damage ticks (zone.every is in the snapshot). Each strike is only the 'arrow_impact' sprite sheet: no chips, no dust, no shaft left in the floor. A see-through draw_circle (1718) covers the field.
findings.should: Volleys land in waves exactly on the ticks. Each arrow kicks up dust and stone chips and leaves a quivering shaft that stands briefly, then breaks.
findings.proposal: Take the volley index k = floor((total-left)/every) from the zone and the spots from _h(id*131 + k*17 + i), so arrows arrive on the tick. On each new k (_tick 'hail:%d'), per arrow: particles.chips + dust_flat, a small particles.floor_crack on one in four, and a splinter emit. Draw the stuck shaft cells for about 0.4 s. Replace the alpha circle with a PixelPaint.disc dither.
findings.check: Confirmed. The 'arrows' look lands each arrow on clock*1.6 + i/count*3, which is not tied to the zone's every (0.5 s for sniper_11 in talents.json). The snapshot zone carries time, total and every, so the volley index can come from the zone. Each strike is only the 'arrow_impact' sprite. _zone_matter skips the arrows look entirely, and _zone_element returns '' for it. The draw_circle at alpha 0.18 is there. The code comment promises 'dust, splinters and a quivering shaft', but none of it is implemented.

findings.title: Arrow and bolt impacts are gold sparks and coin-like chips at a guessed point, never splinters off the surface
findings.element: arrows (sniper gold, beast), mage bolts at walls
findings.now: Archer talent arrows (sniper_1/3/7, beast_6) land through Pal.kind('gold'/'beast'): particles.sparks + chips in gold (gold chips that settle on the floor like coins), whatever they hit, wall or flesh. There are no splinters, no tip spark and no dust, while the enemies' bone arrows do splinter (shot_looks.gd:150-176). The impact point is guessed (777) and the matter goes along -flight instead of bouncing off the wall face. MageBolt.burst (mage_bolt.gd:146) uses s.p, which is already inside the blocked wall cell, so the icicle's splinters and the orb's implosion ring spawn inside the wall.
findings.should: Arrows break as wood and iron: splinters thrown back off the surface, one spark from the tip, a puff of dust; gold only for the glint. Bolts burst at the wall face.
findings.proposal: As proposed. For MageBolt, the simplest fix is in hell_game.gd at the wall branch: compute the contact point once (the same bisection wall_hit does between s.p - s.v*dt and s.p, or have story_feel.wall_hit return the contact and normal) and set s.p to it before calling MageBolt.burst, so the burst needs no dt or blocked lookup of its own. Pass the normal for out_dir.
findings.check: Confirmed. Talent arrows are tracked in draw_bullet before the style check, and element_of(sniper_*) is gold. So _impact paints a burst and _matter throws particles.sparks plus gold chips, whatever they hit. beast_6 gets beast chips plus dust instead, so 'gold' applies only to sniper. The point is guessed (talent_fx.gd:777) and the matter goes along -dir rather than a reflected wall normal. Enemy bone arrows do splinter (ShotLooks.impact). MageBolt.burst uses s.p, which hell_game.gd:2732-2742 has just found inside a blocked cell, and only feel.wall_hit bisects to the contact, so the icicle splinters and the orb ring spawn inside the wall.

findings.title: Monster knockback decays per frame, so throw distance and the Rage slam window change with the frame rate
findings.now: step_body multiplies the push m.k by push.decay 0.86 once per frame, whatever dt is (physics_motion.json:25 even says so). Total travel is about push*dt/0.14. A Rage throw (story_hero.gd:213, 520*1.5*1.2 = 936 px/s) flies about 111 px at 60 Hz, 46 px at 144 Hz and 223 px at 30 Hz. The slam check (push > 330 px/s) lasts 7 frames, so a wall only counts if it is within about 72 px (60 Hz) or 30 px (144 Hz). A sword knock (600*0.25 = 150 px/s) moves an enemy 18 px at 60 Hz but 7 px at 144 Hz. check_slam also hardcodes the decay as m.k / 0.86 (story_hero.gd:222).
findings.should: The same blow should push a body the same distance over the same time at any refresh rate. The Rage slam should trigger at the same wall distance on every machine.
findings.proposal: In step_body use push * pow(decay, dt * 60.0). That keeps today's 60 Hz tuning exactly. Better: a new physics_motion.json push.half_life_s of 0.077 and push * exp2(-dt / half_life). Return the pre-decay push as "push_in" in the result. Let story_hero.check_slam read that value instead of m.k / 0.86, so retuning decay never breaks the slam. Callers to check: hell_monsters.gd:536-543 and hell_game.gd:2930-2935.
findings.check: Confirmed. motion_kit.gd:163 returns push * decay (0.86) once per step, with no dt in it, and physics_motion.json push._note says so in plain words. hell_game._process only caps dt at 0.05. project.godot sets no max_fps and no physics tick, so the game runs once per vsync frame. Travel works out to push*dt/(1-0.86): about 111 px at 60 Hz and 46 px at 144 Hz for the 936 px/s Rage throw. check_slam (story_hero.gd:222) hardcodes m.k / 0.86. Both callers write m.k = step.push: hell_monsters.gd:543 and hell_game.gd:2935. The proposal is right: pow(decay, dt*60) keeps the 60 Hz tuning, and returning push_in for check_slam removes the hardcoded 0.86.

findings.title: Hölle bodies freeze where they died, play one death row and vanish after 0.75 s
findings.now: 13 of the 18 Hölle monster defs have no part rig (hell_rigs.json only has the drakes and blutfledermaus). Their corpse (line 575) is pinned to m.p. It plays the death row once (draw_corpse 1978-1986) and is filtered out at c.t >= 0.75, so the body just disappears and only the blood stain stays. The killing blow's momentum m.k is dropped, and so is enemy.tumble from the Urknall: _sprite only applies pose.lean, never a rotation. The Frostgruft fallback for unrigged looks (story_feel.gd FALL_TIME 0.45) flattens, tips 0.35 rad and fades. Krypta rigs, by contrast, ragdoll and leave pieces lying (cap 60).
findings.should: A felled body should keep moving with the blow: slide or skid with friction, stop at walls, turn over if it was spinning. It should end up lying on the floor and fade slowly, as the Krypta ragdoll pieces do.
findings.proposal: Keep the dissolve and its 0.75 s life. At line 575 store v = m.k and spin = the tumble rate in the corpse dict. Note that after a Rage slam or a photon kill m.k is 0, so fall back to the direction from _kill_fx(m) times a small speed by tier. In the corpse loop (1694), move c.p with MotionKit.integrate against a box_blocked solid and friction v *= exp(-8*dt). Then c.p carries the momentum and stops at walls. Draw with an angle: pass {lean: c.ang} as the pose in draw_corpse, easing the angle from the tumble toward 0. Optionally emit the dissolving pixels as embers or ash particles through _phys().emit with the corpse velocity, so the matter drifts on with the blow. Do not hold or extend the last frame.
findings.check: The code matches the claim. hell_rigs.json has only drache1-4 and blutfledermaus, and no hell_monsters.json def has a 'rig' key. Corpses are pinned at m.p (hell_monsters.gd:575) and filtered at c.t < 0.75 (line 1696). draw_corpse plays the death row over 0.75 s, and _sprite applies only pose.lean, so m.k and m.tumble are dropped. But the atlas (kettenschinder.png row 3) is a deliberate disintegration into red and ember pixels. The body is meant to dissolve, not lie down. 'Hold the last frame 6 s and end up lying like Krypta pieces' would go against the art. The real defect is smaller: the dissolve stays exactly where the body died and ignores the momentum and spin of the killing blow.

findings.title: Talent hits replace the knockback with 60 px/s away from the hero, ignoring where the blast was
findings.now: _damage_enemy assigns m.k = direction * 60, and direction is hero→enemy (talent_combat.gd:1196 and 1201). That holds even for area blasts, where `away` from _blast_at is computed one line later but only goes into the ragdoll stamp. Meteor, Nova and the Urknall collapse therefore move living enemies about 7 px. An enemy standing between the hero and the impact is pushed toward the blast centre. Because the push is assigned rather than added, every talent zone tick resets a running push (for example a 520 px/s wave_at shove) to 60 px/s. Every photon beam tick goes through _damage_mob(m, Vector2.ZERO) (hero_kit.gd:575) and sets m.k = 0 (hell_game.gd:1984), stopping the body dead in mid-flight. The Rage slam damage does the same (story_hero.gd:229).
findings.should: Explosions should push bodies outward from their own centre, with force scaled to the blast (an ultimate throws, a tick does not). Impulses should add up, and a damage-over-time tick or a beam should never cancel a flight that is already running.
findings.proposal: As proposed: pass `away` and an impulse by tier into _damage_enemy, add instead of assign, and skip the push for zone and DoT ticks and when push == ZERO in hell_game._damage_mob. Two additions. (1) Clamp the summed push, for example m.k = (m.k + J).limit_length(push_max), with push_max of about 1000 px/s in physics_motion.json, so stacked multi-hits never fling bodies across rooms. (2) Treat larger ultimate pushes (320/520 px/s) as a balance change: they push enemies out of their own lingering zones, such as the meteor crater and Singularity fields. Tune them low first, or apply them only to the tier's kill or final blow. Leave the Rage slam's own m.k = 0 (story_hero.gd:231) as it is: stopping at the wall is intended.
findings.check: Confirmed. hell_talents.gd:477 assigns m.k = direction * 60 (12 for a boss). Here direction is hero→enemy (talent_combat.gd:1196 and 1201), while 'away' from _blast_at goes only into _stamp. Zone ticks call _hit and then _damage_enemy with feedback=true (talent_combat.gd:1575), so every tick resets m.k. The photon beam calls g._damage_mob(m, ZERO), which sets m.k = ZERO*0.25 = 0 (hero_kit.gd:575, hell_game.gd:1984). One correction: wave_at is called only from the debug Testraum, so the '520 px/s wave_at shove' example is not reached in normal play. Real flights such as the Rage throw (936 px/s) and the explosion push (story_elements.gd:407) are still reset.

findings.title: Frostgruft ragdolls scatter randomly, fly through walls and never tumble
findings.now: FrostRigs._entry builds the renderer entry without "kill" (direction, tier, element) and without "tumble". RigRenderer._kill_of therefore gets a zero direction, and _detach launches every part in a random direction at tier small: a sword kill blows parts toward the hero just as often as away. The Frostgruft renderer never gets `solid`. Only drake_rig_host.bind_world sets it, called from hell_monsters.gd:576. RigDebris.solid is therefore 'never', and severed parts and ragdoll pieces fly through walls. Urknall-flung figures stay upright because rig_renderer.gd:555 reads enemy.tumble. In Krypta and Hölle the walls are only bound at the first corpse, so parts cut off a living figure before any kill also pass through walls.
findings.should: Parts should fly away from the killing blow with the blow's force and element, bounce off walls, and flung figures should turn over, as they do in Krypta.
findings.proposal: In _entry add e.kill: m.hit_fx when it is less than 600 ms old (the talent stamp), else {dx, dy} from m.k or m.feel_dir (story_feel.on_hit sets it), with tier "small" and element from statuses (copy hell_monsters._kill_fx). Add e.tumble = m.tumble. In FrostRigs._init, set renderer.solid = func(p): return g.box_blocked(Rect2(p - Vector2(2, 2), Vector2(4, 4))). In the hell world, call drake_rig.bind_world once in load_floor instead of at the first corpse.
findings.check: Confirmed. FrostRigs._entry (frost_rigs.gd:137-160) writes no 'kill' and no 'tumble'. RigRenderer._kill_of then gets a zero dir and tier 'small', and RigDebris.launch with dir ZERO scatters at random (rig_debris.gd:284-286). renderer.solid is set only by drake_rig_host.bind_world (called at hell_monsters.gd:576 on the first corpse) and never for FrostRigs, so DebrisLook.solid is always false and Frostgruft debris ignores walls. rig_renderer.gd:555 reads enemy.tumble, which the frost entry lacks. The proposal is feasible: FrostRigs draws in world px, the same space as box_blocked.

findings.title: Frostgruft body contact, dashers and the Golem's charge never knock the hero back
findings.now: In the Frostgruft mob path, touch damage calls _hurt(..., m.p, m) and never calls frost_fx.knock. The dasher's dash (2876) and the kit boss charge (boss_kit.gd:229-238) hurt only through this path. A charging Frost Golem runs over the hero without moving him. In Krypta and Hölle, the same touch goes through _hurt_by(..., "contact"/"dash") and pushes him at 300/560 px/s * 0.7. frost_theme.json vfx.knock also has no "contact" entry.
findings.should: A body blow should shove the hero away from the attacker in every world, and harder for a dash or charge.
findings.proposal: After the _hurt call, check whether it landed (state.inv rose and perfect_now() is false). If so, call frost_fx.hit_hero(m.p, "dash" if m.dash > 0 or m.busy.do == "charge" else "contact", "small", m.kind == "boss"). Add "contact": 300 to frost_theme.json vfx.knock.
findings.check: Confirmed. In the Frostgruft mob loop (hell_game.gd:2942-2946), touch damage calls _hurt(..., m.p, m). _hurt (1446) and _lose_hp have no knock, and the only frost knocks are frost_fx.hit_hero calls in frost_moves._hit_hero and the eshot path (2828). The basic 'dasher' behaviour (2876) and the BossKit 'charge' (boss_kit.gd:229-236) deal damage only through this contact path. frost_theme.json vfx.knock has a 'dash' entry (560) but no 'contact'. The proposal is feasible. To detect a landed hit, compare state.hp before and after, as frost_moves._hit_hero does; checking inv also fires when a shield charge is used up.

findings.title: Boss shockwaves push the hero only when they damage him, and never push monsters or gas
findings.now: A wave only counts as a hit when z.dmg > 0, and the knock happens only inside _hurt_by when the damage actually lands (line 311: open and inv rose). During the 0.9 s of invulnerability after any hit, which is common in boss fights, a stomp ring passes through the hero without moving him. frost_moves._hit_hero has the same gate (`if hp >= before: return`). The wave front shoves pixels, embers and lava (_blow_front 3117) but never g.gas: hell_monsters has no gas.impulse call at all. It also never shoves the boss's adds or corpses. The hero's own wave reaction (story_elements.wave_at 631-660) does blow gas away and pushes monsters.
findings.should: A pressure front should shove everything it crosses, whatever the damage rules say: the hero (damage stays gated), non-kit monsters by mass, and gas clouds.
findings.proposal: Leave the hero knock gated on damage (i-frame knock immunity is intended), and do not add new gas impulses at blast origins, since kick already covers them. In the 'wave' case, each frame, give every non-kit, non-boss monster (skip z.m) whose distance lies in the band [z.blown, front] a push: m.k += away * blow.push * share * fall. Set a per-zone 'shoved' id set so each body is pushed once per front. Optionally, to make the gas follow the moving front, call g.gas.impulse(z.p, front, 0.3) once when the front passes half its radius. Treat shoving the boss's own adds as a gameplay change and keep the push small, for example 0.5 of blow.push.
findings.check: Partly confirmed. The hero knock is gated on landed damage (hell_monsters.gd:311, frost_moves.gd:438-440), but that is deliberate: knockback immunity during i-frames is a standard anti-juggle rule. The claim that waves never move gas is mostly wrong. gas is registered as a particle 'liquid' layer (story_feel.gd:641, hell_game.gd:3338), so every particles.kick, including _phys_blast at hell_monsters.gd:1030, 1095, 1651, 1657 and 1684 and the feedback impacts, calls gas.ripple_near and then gas_field.impulse(radius*1.4). Only the front's _blow_front uses P.blow and moves no gas. What is really missing is that wave, erupt and land fronts never push other monsters or corpses.

findings.title: Thrown bodies end badly: Urknall flights stop dead and snap upright, Rage slam kills rebound the wrong way, dash and charge wall hits are silent
findings.now: (1) _step_flung moves flung enemies at a constant 760 px/s until fling_m is used up. _flight_over then erases tumble, so the body stops from full speed in one frame and snaps upright. (2) The Rage slam calls _damage_mob(m, Vector2.ZERO) and then sets m.k = 0 (story_hero.gd:229-231). A kill there has no hit_fx, so _kill_fx (hell_monsters.gd:4072) falls back to the hero→body direction, which points into the wall, at tier small with no wall flag. Parts fly into the wall instead of off it, and nothing calls particles.wall_splat or splat_burst; only Urknall wall kills do (talent_fx.gd:2411). (3) A Frostgruft dash that hits a wall (frost_moves.gd:357-362) and the Golem's charge (boss_kit.gd:234-235) just stop, with no dust, shake or recoil.
findings.should: Flights should slow down, skid and land, with the spin easing into a lying pose. A body slammed into a wall should splat on it and rebound or come apart away from it. A charging body that hits a wall should crunch and recoil.
findings.proposal: Fling and Rage-slam proposals as given, with one fix to the landing. A flung enemy that survives keeps walking, so do not ease tumble to the nearest multiple of PI: one landing upside down would walk on upside down. Ease it to the nearest multiple of TAU over about 0.25 s, so it rolls back upright, then erase it. The landing hop can be a short visual z-offset only. For the speed falloff, store fly.total at _fling_caught and use speed * sqrt(left/total), with a floor of about 0.25. The thrown distance stays the same, so the wall-kill gameplay does not change. Dash and charge wall hit: fx, a small recoil and keeping stun_on_wall are fine.
findings.check: Confirmed on all three points. (1) _step_flung moves at a constant fling_speed until fly.left is used up, and _flight_over erases tumble (talent_combat.gd:2548), so the body stops dead and snaps upright. (2) check_slam calls _damage_mob(m, ZERO) and sets m.k = 0. On a kill, _kill_fx finds no fresh hit_fx and falls back to m.p - hero, which points into the wall, at tier small with no wall flag. Nothing calls splat_burst or wall_splat; only the Urknall's _splat_physics does. (3) The frost_moves dash wall hit (357-362) and the BossKit charge (234-235) just stop, with no fx. wall_splat and splat_burst exist in particles.gd, and vfx_gore ragdoll.tiers has 'splat'.

findings.title: Hero death freezes shots, rigs and debris in mid-air while particles keep moving
findings.now: While state.dead > 0 (1.8 s), _update returns before _update_shots, _update_mobs, frost_rigs.frame, drake_rig.frame, _update_zones and _step_elements. feel.update still runs, so feedback.particles keeps stepping. For the whole death beat, enemy bolts hang in the air, ragdoll pieces and severed parts stop mid-flight, and pools and gas stop. Meanwhile blood, dust and embers keep flying and settling around them.
findings.should: Either everything moves on and only AI and damage stop, or everything slows down together in a uniform slow motion. Some matter frozen while other matter moves reads as a bug.
findings.proposal: Prefer the passive step, with damage strictly off. Move the eshots and the hero shots and run their wall impacts without hurt or mob damage, so nothing grants exp after death. Run frost_rigs.frame and drake_rig.frame (debris only), corpse aging (the corpse loop in monsters.update only, no AI), _step_gas, pools.sync and the frost_fx and knock aging. If that is too intrusive, the cheap alternative is one global slow-motion factor applied to everything, particles included, through feel.update's dt.
findings.check: Confirmed. hell_game._update returns in the state.dead branch (2540-2550) after only feel.update and the music, so _update_shots, _update_mobs (with monster corpses and debris), frost_rigs.frame, drake_rig.frame, _update_zones, frost_fx.update and the gas step all stop for 1.8 s. The feel's particles keep stepping, so mixed frozen and moving matter is visible during the death beat.

findings.title: Frostgruft boss pushes teleport the hero, the vortex pull sticks at walls, and Unbezwingbar's knockback immunity is never applied
findings.now: _push_hero moves the hero int(dist/16) steps of 16 px within a single frame, so he jumps 160 px instantly. It runs at every phase break (line 80) wherever he stands in the room, with no range check and no falloff, and at teleport_center (244). The vortex pull (frost_moves.gd:383-389) applies the full vector or nothing, so on a diagonal pull the hero gets stuck at walls and corners instead of sliding along them. The chain pull uses MotionKit.move_hero axis by axis. talent_combat.cc_immune (885; Unbezwingbar promises 'no knockback') is read nowhere. MotionKit.knock_hero, the chain pull (hell_monsters.gd:1765), the vortex and _push_hero all still move him.
findings.should: Boss pushes should be eased knockbacks that weaken with distance and slide along walls. Pulls should slide along walls. An active knockback immunity should stop every forced move.
findings.proposal: Replace _push_hero with an eased knock, but keep the distance. The 'wave' entry in frost_theme (600 px/s, 0.22 s) covers only about 44 px, against today's 160. Build a table per call: {'push': 3*dist*falloff/T, 'time': T} with T of about 0.35. At dist 160 that is about 1370 px/s, under knock.step_max*60. Use falloff = clamp(1 - d/r, 0.3, 1), skip beyond r, and call _mover().knock_hero(from, 'push', table, false). Move the vortex with motion_kit().move_hero(pull). Add hero_immovable() to StoryMotionHost (g.talents != null and g.talents.tc.cc_immune(1)). Gate knock_hero, the vortex and chain pulls, and _push_hero on it, but not the hero's own step_hero walking.
findings.check: Confirmed. boss_kit._push_hero moves the hero int(dist/16) steps of 16 px inside one call, for example 160 px in a single frame. It runs at every phase break with no range check or falloff (line 80), and at teleport_center (with a 160 px check). The frost_moves vortex (383-389) applies the full pull vector or nothing, with no per-axis slide. talent_combat.cc_immune is read only in the old src/game.gd. The Bollwerk text in talents.json promises immunity to stun and knockback ('immun gegen Betäubung und Rückstoß'), yet nothing in the story worlds checks it.

findings.title: Knockback ignores body size, and thrown bodies pass through crowds without transferring momentum
findings.now: Push factors know only boss or not boss. The sword pushes every mob at 0.25*600 = 150 px/s whether it is a Glutimp (r 24) or a Kettenschinder (r 38). The wave reaction pushes bosses at half of 520 px/s (story_elements.gd:651), so a Drache4 (r 190) slides about 31 px from a wave but 3.6 px from a sword. holy_at (713) pushes bosses at full strength with no share. Mob separation (hell_monsters.gd:527, hell_game.gd:2909) is a constant soft 120 px/s, so a body thrown at 936 px/s (Rage) or 760 px/s (Urknall) passes straight through a pack without hitting anyone.
findings.should: The same impulse should move a light body far and a heavy one little, consistently for every source. A fast body that hits another should hand over part of its momentum, like bowling pins, and Rage throws into a crowd should knock others down.
findings.proposal: Add MotionKit.impulse(m, J) with a mass normalized to the typical mob. Use mass = clamp((r / r_ref)^2, 0.4, 4), where r_ref is the median of the current non-boss st.r values, so mid-size mobs keep today's pushes and balance shifts only at the extremes. Kit bosses stay immovable. Route _damage_mob, hell_talents, story_elements explode (407) and sub_kit:643 through it. Leave the Rage throw as a fixed throw speed that is already restricted to non-bosses. Do momentum transfer only for bodies that carry m.slam or are in talent_combat.flung, inside the existing O(n²) separation loop: on overlap, along the normal, with restitution about 0.4 and split by mass. This keeps the cost and the behaviour change local.
findings.check: Confirmed for gameplay paths. hell_game.gd:1984 pushes 0.25*push for every non-boss whatever its size, hell_talents pushes a flat 60 (12 for a boss), and the separation loops add a flat 120 px/s soft push (hell_monsters.gd:527, hell_game.gd:2909), with no momentum transfer. Thrown bodies (Rage, story_hero.gd:213; the Urknall moves through _move/_shove) pass through packs. One correction: wave_at and holy_at are called only from the debug Testraum (story_testraum_tools.gd:308-314), so the wave and holy examples do not apply in normal play.

findings.title: On ice a knockback stops as fast as on stone
findings.now: The hero's knock is a separate eased displacement (knock_step) that ends after 0.22 s on any floor. It never touches player.vel, so on glaze ice (grip 0.015) a frost wave stops him as dead as on stone, even though his own walking keeps sliding for seconds. frost_snow.sliding() and slide_lean() (brother's file) key on player.vel, so a knock across ice leaves no skid marks and no lean. Monsters work the same way: push decays at 0.86 per frame whatever their grip (line 163), and only their walking slides.
findings.should: A blow on slippery ground should send a body gliding away with its momentum, then the grip slows it down, and the boots should skid and lean.
findings.proposal: Hero: as proposed. When the grip under him at knock start is below FIRM, add knock.v times about 0.6 to player.vel once and clear the eased knock. step_hero's slide and the brother's skid marks then follow without touching frost_snow.gd. Monsters: do not decay push with pow(grip, dt) on glaze. At grip 0.015 a Rage throw would glide over 200 px. Use a softened grip for the push, for example pow(max(grip, push.ice_floor 0.12), dt), together with the frame-rate-independent decay from finding #0. Keep frost-tagged creatures FIRM as now.
findings.check: Confirmed. step_knock and knock_step (motion_kit.gd:86-124) move the hero by an eased displacement that ends at knock.T and never touch host.hero_velocity, so on glaze or ice the knock stops as on stone. frost_snow.sliding() and slide_lean() (src/hero/frost_snow.gd:136-148, brother's file, unchanged by the fix) key on player.vel only. For monsters, step_body decays push by a fixed factor regardless of grip.

findings.title: Monster wall collision: velocity into a wall is kept, bodies get stuck inside solids, and large steps can pass through thin props
findings.now: step_body returns vel: kept and push even when integrate blocked an axis, while the hero's step_hero zeroes it. On ice, a monster that slid into a wall keeps pressing into it for up to about 1 s, running in place. integrate cannot leave a solid it starts in, because both axis tests fail. That happens when the Singularity orbit `_shove`s enemies to core positions without a collision check (talent_combat.gd:1962), or when a gravity or ice wall is spawned over them (hero_kit.gd:710, sub_kit.gd:293, via mob_solid → wall_blocks). Those enemies stay embedded until the wall expires, or for good when parked inside a wall cell. There is no step cap for monsters: 936 px/s at the 0.05 s dt cap is a 47 px step, larger than a 30 px crate or brazier plus a small mob box (rr 14). The chain pull moves the hero at 1100 px/s, 55 px per frame (hell_monsters.gd:1765), bypassing knock.step_max = 24. The leap slam lerps its position and tests only the sampled points (hell_monsters.gd:1069-1071), so it can hop through wall cells.
findings.should: A body that hits a wall should lose the velocity component into it (or bounce), get pushed out when something solid appears around it, and never skip a solid in one step.
findings.proposal: Have integrate report hit_x and hit_y. Important: zeroing the push on a blocked axis would break the Rage slam, because check_slam detects the wall hit from m.k / 0.86 being still large while the body did not move. So first add 'push_in' and 'hit' to the step_body result (see finding #0) and let check_slam use them. After that, zero kept on the blocked axis, and push too, or reflect it by about 0.2. Add depenetration: if solid(p) holds at the start, try the 8 directions at rr and 2*rr and move to the first free one. Use talent_move instead of a raw _shove in _catch_step. March the leap path in roughly 8 px samples from the last position and stop at the first blocked sample. Substepping integrate and the chain pull above step_max is cheap insurance but low priority, since it matters only at 20 fps or less.
findings.check: Partly confirmed. step_body returns vel: kept and the push unchanged even when integrate blocked an axis, whereas step_hero zeroes the blocked axis. integrate cannot depenetrate. talent_combat._catch_step _shoves enemies onto orbit points with no collision test (1962). Gravity and ice walls (hero_kit.gd:710, sub_kit.gd:293) are tested through wall_blocks in mob_solid, so a body under a new wall stays stuck. The leap lerp (hell_monsters.gd:1066-1069) can hop a wall cell, since L.to is the hero's position. The tunnelling claim is overstated. The mob box is 2*rr wide, so passing through a 30 px prop on x needs a step of at least 58 px, more than the 47 px maximum at the 0.05 dt cap. Only y at 20 fps or less, and the chain pull at 20 fps or less (55 px), can skip. These are low-fps edge cases.

findings.title: Talent spells never touch walls, props or crates
findings.now: Since 29.10 keys 1-4 cast talents, and talents are the main spells. A talent bolt (fire bolt, ice lance, arrow) that reaches a wall is dropped in _step_bullets (talent_blocked → bullets.remove_at) with no wall_hit: no bite, no chips, no dust, no sparks. It simply vanishes at the stone. Talent explosions, novas and meteor craters (talent_combat.gd:2499 _event) call only _element. They never call wreck.blast, so candles, bones and urn props right beside a Meteor stay whole and the walls show no wear. A legacy fireball shot (_explode → wreck.blast) or an enemy slam (story_feel.on_blast) does bite walls and shatter props.
findings.should: Every spell is matter hitting the world. A bolt hitting stone chips it in its element: fire scorches and leaves embers, ice shatters into shards that lie as frost, void throws motes. Explosions bite the nearest wall faces and blow props apart, scaled by radius, the same way as every other blast source.
findings.proposal: Bolts: do NOT call g.feel.wall_hit. It raises a second crypt wall_hit burst on top of talent_fx's inferred impact, which doubles the matter. When talent_blocked ended the bolt, wear the wall only: g.wreck.hit_line(from, b.pos + v.normalized()*16, style, owner). hit_line already bisects to the contact and goes through wreck.wall_hit, so a hero bolt hitting a smashable prop also breaks it. If the blocking box is an unbroken breakable (test _breakable_box(e).intersects), call g._hit_breakable(e, b.pos) with wreck.hit_dir = v. Style map as proposed. Explosions: in hell_talents.update, walk tc.snapshot().events with a seen-id set. For kind in [explosion, nova, impact] with r >= blast.min_radius, call g.wreck.blast(at, r, 'blast', owner > 0) plus the breakables hook from #2. Skip events that hell_game raises through tc.show_effect for the pyro shot (hell_game:2741/3069), because _explode already blasted there. Tag them with extra {'wrecked': true} and skip that tag.
findings.check: Partly true. The core claim holds. hell_talents._step_bullets:543-554 drops a bolt that hits a wall (talent_blocked uses g.box_blocked, which also covers solids and unbroken breakables) and calls nothing on the wreck. talent_combat._event:2489 sends nova/explosion/impact only to _element, so props, walls and crates are never hit. wreck.blast is called only from hell_game:3062, hell_monsters:2669 and story_feel:194. A bolt stopped by a crate also never hits it. The 'simply vanishes, no chips, no sparks' part is wrong. talent_fx.draw_bullet records every talent shot (_track_shot), and _settle_shots:753 turns a shot that vanishes into _impact. That spawns ember_sparks plus a scorch for fire, shatter plus rime for ice, an implosion for void, element matter and residue. What is missing at the wall is the wear (bite, crack, chips from story_wreck), not the burst.

findings.title: Pixel particles fly through closed gates, pillars and crates
findings.now: particles.solid() only knows the walkable cells that story_feel._set_floor:791 hands it (every cell where _walkable(t) is true). findings.title: World embers and _burst are straight-line squares spawned per frame
findings.now: hell_game.embers is a second particle system without physics: p += v*dt, with no gravity, floor, walls or buoyancy. _burst (2198) throws n of them with v in [-150..150]x[-210..90]. They fly in straight lines (some downward, some through walls) and vanish after 0.35-0.85 s. _burst is used everywhere: every hero blast (_explode:3073, 18 squares), icicle impacts (3036), wells, mimics, level-ups, boss phases (boss_kit 81/242/255), boss deaths (hell_monsters:1570, 160 gold squares, plus 1563 randf()<0.5 per frame for 14 more). Ambient lava embers spawn int(W.theme.embers) samples (2..7) per FRAME (3176) and rise at constant speed. At 144 Hz that is 2.4x the 60 Hz density, and the 360 cap (3189) slices off the oldest at full alpha, so embers blink out mid-rise. Vents (3097, randf()<0.6) and the vault (4049, emitted inside _draw_ent, which keeps running during hitstop) are per-frame chances too.

The feel's particles already do all of this (ember_sparks, glut, chips). Emission is a rate per second.
findings.proposal: As proposed. When routing _burst into particles, convert units (at / feel.scale) and cap with P.room(n). Keep _burst's early-return for the feel level-up. Krypta/Frostgruft tints come from col('ember'/'ember_big'), which are green and blue in the themes. For the Krypta's ambient Moder 'embers', follow #1 and emit miasma motes/drops instead of buoyant embers.
findings.check: Confirmed. _update_embers:3174 appends int(W.theme.embers) (2..7 from world_core:137) per frame, with no dt scaling. Its step is p += v*dt plus push, with no gravity, floor or wall. The 360 cap slices off the oldest (alpha = min(1, t*2), so they are still opaque). _burst:2198 throws v in [-150,150]x[-210,90] squares with no physics and is called from about 40 sites, including the boss death at hell_monsters:1563 (randf()<0.5 per frame) and :1570 (160). Vent embers at 3097 and the vault at 4049 are per-frame randf chances, and the vault one is emitted inside a draw function. Drawn as squares at 3881.

findings.title: Snow melts only under fire bowls; fire and blasts leave it untouched
